core.title: Delegate train execution from the InterlockingRunner to the TrainRunner; never execute wagons in interlocking code
core.given: An application module defines an InterlockingRunner (route control)
core.when: you add or change anything in that module (imports, action handling, train execution)
core.then: Resolve one admissible train and delegate its execution to the TrainRunner's execute entry point (roles.runtime_components#train_runner_execute); the InterlockingRunner must never execute wagons itself.
prefer: Delegate instead of executing: resolve the admissible train for the action, then hand that train to the TrainRunner and return the result of its execution — do not loop over the steps yourself
avoid: Importing a wagon entry module anywhere in the InterlockingRunner module
Invoking a direct train-execution entry point from interlocking code

Iterating a train's step sequence — its ordered steps — as an executor loop; the sequence containment field and the executor-loop idiom are per-stack profile data (roles.plan_hierarchy#train_step_sequence, idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop)
Otherwise invoking wagon steps, choosing the next step inside a train, or bypassing the TrainRunner
unless: The production TrainRunner itself is the legitimate wagon-step executor; its own step loop is exempt
core.why: Interlocking is route control, not execution: the TrainRunner is the single component that runs wagons and carries Cargo between them; a second executor would compete with it.
evidence: The stack's direct-execution check reports no direct-execution finding in any InterlockingRunner-defining module
The InterlockingRunner's execute path returns the result of delegating the resolved train to the TrainRunner's execute entry point (roles.runtime_components#train_runner_execute)
verification: Strict disposition, severity 4: a newly introduced direct-execution pattern is not suppressible and fails the check run.

The check flags, in any InterlockingRunner-defining module: a direct import of a wagon entry module, a call of a direct train-execution entry point, and a step-sequence iteration used as an executor loop. How these patterns are recognized concretely is the per-stack detector's concern (profile: layout.locations#wagon_entry, roles.runtime_components#direct_train_execution, roles.plan_hierarchy#train_step_sequence, idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop).
The check exempts the production TrainRunner itself: its own step loop is legitimate and not flagged. Which module is the TrainRunner is the per-stack detector's concern.

Scope: every InterlockingRunner-defining module wherever it lives in the application. Which trees a detector actually scans is the per-stack realization's concern; a narrower scan path (the trains tree in the reference realization) is a detector-scope limitation, not part of the obligation.

fires: Adding or editing any InterlockingRunner-defining module in the application, wherever it lives
An InterlockingRunner-defining module gains an import of a wagon entry module, anywhere in the module
Interlocking code invokes a direct train-execution entry point or iterates a train's step sequence to run steps
doesNotFire: Editing the production TrainRunner itself, including its own step loop
Changes to wagon modules or other code that never defines an InterlockingRunner
A tree with no InterlockingRunner at all (covered by the companion rule that requires one to exist)

neutralityNotes: InterlockingRunner, TrainRunner, wagon, train, step sequence and Cargo are the ATDD runtime's own architecture vocabulary (agnostic core spec afokapu/atdd#1251), not stack names, so the core keeps them; it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path. Everything concrete about recognizing the forbidden patterns is per-stack profile data: the wagon entry module (layout.locations#wagon_entry), the direct-execution call (roles.runtime_components#direct_train_execution), the train's step-sequence containment field (roles.plan_hierarchy#train_step_sequence) and the executor-loop syntax (idiom.source_syntax#step_executor_loop); the TrainRunner's execution entry point that the positive delegation requires is roles.runtime_components#train_runner_execute. How a detector recognizes those constructs in code remains the per-stack realization's concern. The reference detector's src/trains/** scan scope is narrower than the app-wide obligation; bun.json itself states the path is not a prerequisite, so the core stays app-wide. The language activation fact (typescript/javascript) is stack profile data (tooling.languages) that the realization uses for language gating; 'language' is not a neutral fact kind, so the neutral core does not gate on it. The doesNotFire cross-reference to coder.bun.interlocking-runner-exists was neutralized to 'the companion rule that requires an InterlockingRunner to exist', since rule ids are realization-scoped.
